studies.dataset_observation_period: YouTube channel/video/comment observation through February 2023; described as June 2020 to February 2023
studies.selection: Authors' large-scale analyzed anglophone political channels, videos and comments, not the whole YouTube platform
studies.methods: quantitative descriptive study of channels, videos, comments and commenter activity

observations.denominator: commenters in selected anglophone political channel sample

limits: A prolific commenter is not necessarily a unique voter, political supporter or representative audience member.
The paper's abstract does not support a global number of political commenters or a precise share beyond 'just over 2%'.
The observed association between posting frequency and coded toxicity cannot be extrapolated to all topics or a personalized behavior prediction.

The Cardiff landing-page abstract reverses the toxicity comparison. The linked author manuscript's abstract, page 21 analysis and Figure 11 consistently place higher coded toxicity among more active commenters; the discrepancy is recorded.
The Perspective API score is classifier-based and may be biased or inaccurate; activity association is neither a personal diagnosis nor proof that frequent participation causes toxicity.

source_variant_conflict.bibliography_abstract: Cardiff ORCA landing-page abstract describes higher toxicity among infrequent commenters.
source_variant_conflict.author_manuscript_abstract: Authors' journal-formatted PDF page 1 describes higher toxicity among superusers.
source_variant_conflict.author_manuscript_body: Authors' journal-formatted PDF page 21 describes higher Perspective API toxicity among more active commenters, consistent with Figure 11 on page 22.

studies.language_scope: At least 90% of comments English, by study inclusion
studies.selection: Top 200 search hits for climate change in March 2021, filtered to videos with >=200 comments, 90% or more comments in English, and alignment with scientific consensus; final 129 videos
studies.methods: video presenter/framing hand-coding and supervised NLP on comments, thread vs. independent comment comparison
limits: English, engagement-threshold and consensus selection exclude much climate content and distort representativeness.
Automated classifiers and manual codes estimate attitudes from comments, not identities, actual beliefs or causal effects.
Videos are source-query based from 2021, not a fresh randomized sample of 2026 topics.

studies.language_scope: Study does not supply population-wide language distribution or independent commenter home countries
studies.selection: 393 pre-recorded public videos with 'study with me' title-search inclusion as of September 2024 and 164,611 analyzed public comments; title-based, not all education videos
studies.methods: selected public-video title-search retrieval; topic modeling and automated sentiment labels on visible comment events
limits: Selected prerecorded Study With Me video titles are not representative of all education videos, study sessions, students or live streams.
Visible comment messages are event counts and may include repeated users; 164,611 does not measure unique commenters or students.
More than 400 million published video-view events from sample videos are not the number of learning viewers, study outcomes or paying community members.
Topic and sentiment categories come from automated text classification, not verified psychological wellbeing or academic progress.
No randomized video design intervention, comment moderation cost, causal social reinforcement, creator earnings or comment-language population was observed.
No real usernames, text bodies, channel identifiers or private audience records are imported into Mercata.

prohibit: Do not infer commenter sex, gender identity, age, ethnicity, religion, partisanship or psychological traits from posts.
Do not store usernames, comment strings, channel identifiers, raw comment ID lists or deduplication keys in public artifacts.
Do not use descriptive findings to design targeted political persuasion or individual manipulation.
Do not sum sample counts across studies or treat study-selected toxicity scores as interchangeable measures.
Do not claim that replies cause more constructive conversations from correlations alone.
Do not generalize anglophone politics or selected English-language climate videos to all YouTube communities or countries.
Do not imply that visible public comments represent all viewers or the community's true opinion distribution.
No cross-topic claim that sentiment positivity in Study With Me equals a viewer-level wellbeing, learning or retention effect.
Do not pool political-channel commenter activity, climate reply sentiment and Study With Me selected visible comment topics as the same population or rate.
followup_method: Use only properly licensed public or consented aggregate corpora and preregistered non-identifying categories; report discovered, sampled, moderated and deleted-comment selection as distinct limitations.
